name: Basilica and Shrine of Our Lady of Perpetual Help
architect: Schickel & Ditmars; spires by Franz Joseph Untersee
history: Redemptorist priests opened a wooden church on Parker Hill in 1870, with the first Mass on 29 January 1871. The icon of Our Mother of Perpetual Help was installed in May 1871, and cures were soon reported and attributed to her intercession. The present church was dedicated in 1878; its twin spires were added in 1910. Pius XII made it a basilica in 1954.
arch: Romanesque Revival in Roxbury puddingstone quarried just down the street, with two tall spires by Swiss architect Franz Joseph Untersee.
features: Its 1897 Hutchings organ was one of the first in the U.S. to use electric action, which Hutchings invented.
Crutches and braces were left at the shrine as votive offerings.

look.d: Added in 1910, they crown Mission Hill.
The walls are local Roxbury puddingstone, a pebbly conglomerate rock.

fun: Locals still call it "the Mission Church", and the neighborhood Mission Hill is named after it.
journal: Puddingstone and spires on Mission Hill. Crutches left behind say what people felt.
